newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany may have to trim grain crop expectations.
newsitem.headline: Germany may have to trim grain crop expectations.

text.p: German farmers may have to reduce earlier 1997 grain harvest expectations because of lower yields but the final result could still match 1996's 42 million tonnes, the June edition of Toepfer's monthly newsletter said.
But the report from the German grain trader said last year's result would only be achieved if earlier forecasts of a grain area expansion by six percent were verified.
There was an information gap as to the likely area because the six percent rise was based on planting figures recorded last December, Toepfer noted.
Rainfall in early June had not been consistent enough, espececially on light soils in the country's North and North East, and this could result in drought damage, Toepfer said.
Total rain volumes in May were sufficient in the North but rains had been unevenly spread there while in the South, only 50 percent of the long-term average of May rains had been received.
Toepfer last month said the 1997 grain harvest looked highly likely to exceed the 1996 figure.
